newsitem.title: USA: NADBank approves two U.S.-Mexico border projects.
newsitem.headline: NADBank approves two U.S.-Mexico border projects.

text.p: The North American Development Bank board on Monday approved $28.9 million in financing for two environmental projects in Texas and California along the U.S.-Mexico border.

The projects are the first to receive NADBank funding on the U.S. side of the border and among the first in up to $8 billion in infrastructure projects to be financed through NADBank over the next 10 years, said Jeffrey Shafer, U.S. Treasury under secretary for international affairs.

"We will have a total lending guarantee capacity of $2-$3 billion, which we expect to be combined with funds from other sources to do up to $8 billion worth of infrastructure projects," he said after the bank's board met here.

Shafer on Monday was named chairman of NADBank, created in 1994 to finance environmental projects along the U.S.-Mexico border underwritten by the two countries. The financing approved today will be used to build a $24.8 million water treatment plant in Brawley, California and make $4.1 million in improvements to a water supply system in Mercedes, Texas.

Last September, the NADBank board approved its first two projects, an $830,000 water supply and wastewater treatment plant in Naco, Sonora and a $1.1 million wastewater plant in Matamoros, Tamaulipas.
